Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

surprise noun

something unexpected

also a surprise, what a surprise!, unexpected

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.2.69: imprōvīsum atque inopīnātum (Lewis & Short, s.v. inopīnātus)

rēs inopīnāta

an unexpected thing

Latin says what the surprise is: something unexpected, inopīnātum or imprōvīsum. “Unexpectedly” is ex inopīnātō or ex necopīnātō.

Other words

  • mīrum, mīrī n. — a wonder, a surprising thing

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 388

    Something to wonder at: mīrum quantum, nec mīrum (see be surprised).

  • necopīnātus, necopīnāta, necopīnātum — unexpected

    declension · also used · classical · Liv. 39.49: necopīnātum gaudium (Lewis & Short)

    Livy’s word for an unexpected joy or blow.

Examples

  • sapientī nihil imprōvīsum accidere potest, nihil inopīnātum, nihil omnīnō novum

    nothing can come to the wise man unforeseen, nothing unexpected, nothing at all newCic. Tusc. 4.37 (Lewis & Short)

See also surprise, be surprised, amaze.

SourcesLewis & Short: inopinatus · Lewis & Short: necopinatus · Lewis & Short: mirus · Lewis & Short: improvisus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 388.
